about: Controlled vocabulary for every scene in Set-Piece Vault. Each facet lists its allowed values with a definition. 'min'/'max' give how many values a scene carries for that facet. Lists are ordered: the first value is the most important.

scene_type.label: Scene type
scene_type.description: What kind of set-piece this is. Exactly one. fight.* is personal-scale combat between individuals or small groups; battle.* is organised forces (armies, squads, fleets). Choose by what dominates the 30-second window.

values.fight.hand_to_hand: Unarmed or improvised-weapon fighting between individuals or small groups: martial arts, brawls, grappling.
values.fight.blades: Swords, knives, spears, staffs, axes or lightsabers between individuals or small groups (duels, one-vs-many). Not armies.
values.fight.gunfight: Firearms combat at personal or small-group scale: shootouts, standoffs, raids, gun-fu. Not military battles.
values.fight.ring_sport: A sanctioned bout with rules and a referee or crowd: boxing, MMA, kumite, wrestling.
values.fight.superpowered: Combat driven by superpowers, mutant abilities or supernatural powers, at any scale (a superhero team against an army stays here).
values.fight.creature: People fighting a creature, monster or alien at personal scale (not giant monsters vs cities).
values.battle.pre_gunpowder: Armies or warbands fighting mainly with blades, spears, bows and cavalry, in any culture or a fantasy world (ancient Rome, medieval Europe, feudal Japan, Middle-earth).
values.battle.black_powder: Organised battle in the musket and cannon era, roughly 1550-1890: arquebus volleys, line infantry, Napoleonic wars, colonial wars, US Civil War.
values.battle.modern_ground: Ground warfare from 1900 to today: infantry, tanks, artillery, helicopters supporting troops, urban combat.
values.battle.air: Aircraft against aircraft, or air attacks on ground or sea targets: dogfights, bombing runs, missile evasion in combat.
values.battle.naval: Ships or submarines in combat: broadsides, boarding, torpedoes, depth charges.
values.battle.space: Spacecraft, starfighters or fleets in combat in space or orbit.
values.battle.giants: Giant monsters, kaiju, mechs or alien war machines against cities, armies or each other.
values.chase.vehicle: A pursuit with cars, motorcycles, trucks, buses, tanks or trains.
values.chase.foot: A pursuit on foot: running, parkour, rooftop runs, jungle flight (jetpacks and wires count if the chasers are people).
values.chase.air: A pursuit or evasion between helicopters or aircraft outside a declared air battle.
values.race: A competitive race: motorsport, street race, chariot race.
values.stunt.set_piece: A practical stunt is the point of the scene: climbing, hanging, falling, jumping, wing-walking.
values.creature.attack: A creature, monster or infected horde attacks or terrorises people who mostly flee rather than fight.
values.disaster: A natural or man-made catastrophe: earthquake, tsunami, tornado, flood, sinking ship, nuclear blast.
values.vfx.showcase: A signature visual-effects moment that is not mainly a fight or chase: bullet time, folding cities, liquid metal, water creatures.
values.space.travel: Spaceflight without combat: launch, docking, landing, wormholes, journeys through space, first sight of a spacecraft.

tier.description: How essential the scene is as a reference. canon = the ones every filmmaker should know; excellent = among the best of its kind.

values.canon: Canon: routinely on greatest-scene lists, award-defining or widely taught and broken down.
values.excellent: Excellent: a widely praised set-piece with a strong, specific craft lesson; among the best of its kind.
values.replaceable: Replaceable: good but not reference-grade; a better example of the same kind exists.

values.small_group_fight: A few people on each side (roughly 2 to 10 in total), or two against one.
values.one_vs_many: One fighter (or a pair) against a crowd of opponents.
values.team_vs_team: Two organised teams or squads of similar size.
values.massed_battle: Large forces clash across a battlefield.
values.ambush: One side is caught by surprise.
values.assault_raid: Attackers storm a building, position, ship or base.
values.siege: An attack on fortifications or walls (castles, cities, forts).
values.last_stand: A defender holds out against overwhelming numbers.
values.standoff: Weapons drawn, tension before (or instead of) the violence.
values.escape: Getting away from danger, capture or pursuers.
values.bout: A refereed or ritual match with rules.
values.rampage: One force destroys or kills largely unopposed.
values.dogfight: Aircraft or spacecraft manoeuvring against each other.
values.bombardment: Shelling, bombing, artillery or orbital fire on a target.
values.demonstration: A display of power, a test or a skill demonstration.
values.journey: Travel from one place to another (flights, launches, voyages).
values.catastrophe: Destruction unfolding with nobody able to stop it.
values.spectacle: A visual event to be watched rather than a contest.

scale.label: Scale
scale.description: How many participants the action involves.

values.solo: One person against the environment, a machine or gravity (most stunts and journeys).
values.one_vs_many: One or two people against a crowd.
values.medium: About 10 to 100 people (squads, platoons, gangs, villages).
values.army: Hundreds or thousands of fighters on screen.
values.city_scale: A whole city or region is affected (disasters, kaiju).

genre.label: Film genre
genre.description: Genre of the film or series the scene comes from. First value is the primary genre.

values.martial_arts: Martial-arts film (kung fu, silat, muay thai, karate).
values.wuxia: Chinese martial-arts fantasy with heroic swordsmen and wire-assisted feats.
values.samurai_jidaigeki: Japanese period drama with samurai, ronin or ninja.
values.swashbuckler: Sword-and-adventure film, usually European, often romantic.
values.historical_epic: Large-scale drama set in a real historical period.
values.war: War film about real or realistic armed conflict.
values.western: American frontier western (including spaghetti westerns and modern takes).
values.crime: Gangsters, heists gone wrong, cops and criminals.
values.heist: A robbery is the spine of the plot.
values.space_opera: Adventure across space with fleets and alien worlds.
values.monster: Giant monsters, kaiju and creature features.

era.label: Story era
era.description: When the scene takes place in the story (not the release year).

values.ancient: Before 500 AD: Greece, Rome, ancient China, Bronze Age.
values.medieval: 500 to 1499: knights, Vikings, crusades, Mongol empire, Heian to Muromachi Japan.
values.early_modern: 1500 to 1799: Sengoku and early Edo Japan, Ming/Qing China, colonial America, pirates, age of sail.
values.19th_century: 1800 to 1899: Napoleonic wars, wild west, US Civil War, Meiji Japan, Victorian empire.
values.early_20th_century: 1900 to 1938: WWI, prohibition, Republican-era China, silent-film era.
values.near_future: A recognisable future with advanced technology on or near Earth.
values.far_future: A space-faring future far from today.
values.fantasy_world: An invented world with no real date (Middle-earth, Westeros, a galaxy far, far away, mythic lands).

region.label: Region or world
region.description: Where the scene takes place, as the audience perceives it.

values.southeast_asia: Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Cambodia, Philippines, Myanmar.
values.central_asia: Mongolia and the steppes, Afghanistan, Central Asian states.
values.middle_east: Arabian peninsula, Levant, Iraq, Iran, Turkey, Holy Land.
values.southern_europe: Italy, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Mediterranean islands.
values.eastern_europe: Poland, Czechia, Hungary, the Balkans, Ukraine, Belarus.
values.american_frontier: The 19th-century American West and its borderlands (also Mexico in westerns).
values.latin_america: Mexico (outside westerns), Central and South America, the Caribbean.
values.open_ocean: At sea, out of sight of land.
values.sky: High in the sky with no specific land beneath.
values.earth_orbit: In orbit around Earth or near the Moon.
values.alien_world: Another planet or moon (including the Moon's surface).
values.fantasy_world: An invented world (Middle-earth, Westeros, Piltover). Fictional countries placed on Earth use their real region (Wakanda: sub_saharan_africa).
values.unspecified_city: A generic or invented modern city that stands for nowhere in particular.

environment.label: Environment
environment.description: The physical spaces the action moves through.

values.city_street: Streets of a city or town.
values.town_main_street: The main street of a small town (westerns, villages).
values.arena_ring: Boxing rings, arenas, colosseums, tournament halls.
values.train: On or inside a train or subway car.
values.aircraft: Inside or on the outside of an aircraft.
values.airfield: Airports, airfields, runways, carriers' flight decks.
values.ship_deck: On the deck of a ship.
values.spacecraft_interior: Inside a spaceship or space station.
values.skyscraper_exterior: The outside of a tall building.
values.open_sea: The sea's surface away from land.
values.planet_surface: The surface of another world or the Moon.
values.dreamscape: Dreams, visions, abstract or impossible spaces.

values.golden_hour: Low warm sun near sunrise or sunset.
values.not_applicable: No time of day (space, abstract interiors with no outside light).

atmosphere.label: Atmosphere and elements
atmosphere.description: Weather, elements and visual texture in the air. Leave empty for a clear, neutral scene.

values.smoke: Smoke from fire, guns or explosions.
values.storm_wind: Storm, high wind, lightning, rough seas.

mood.label: Mood
mood.description: How the scene feels. First value is the dominant mood.

values.tense: Suspense and dread of what comes next.
values.awe: Wonder at something vast or beautiful.

combatants.label: Who is in the action
combatants.description: The kinds of people or beings driving the action.

values.samurai: Japanese samurai serving a lord or clan.
values.ashigaru_japanese_army: Japanese foot soldiers and feudal armies.
values.kung_fu_fighters: Chinese martial artists (kung fu, wing chun, drunken boxing).
values.wuxia_swordsmen: Wuxia heroes and assassins with gravity-defying skill.
values.korean_warriors: Korean soldiers or warriors before the 20th century.
values.medieval_soldiers: Medieval European infantry, archers, levies, clansmen.
values.gladiators: Gladiators and arena fighters, including arena bouts in fantasy and sci-fi worlds.
values.persian_army: Persian or other ancient Near Eastern armies.
values.musket_infantry: Line infantry with muskets or rifles in the black-powder era.
values.native_warriors: Indigenous warriors (Native American, Zulu, Maya and others).
values.ww2_soldiers: Second World War soldiers, including the Second Sino-Japanese War from 1937.
values.cold_war_soldiers: Soldiers of Korea, Vietnam and other 1946-1991 wars.
values.spies_secret_agents: Spies and secret agents (Bond, Bourne, Hunt).
values.gangsters: Gangsters, mobsters, cartel members, street gangs.
values.triads_yakuza: Triads, yakuza and Asian organised crime.
values.martial_artists_modern: Present-day fighters using martial arts (silat, muay thai, MMA).
values.starfighter_pilots: Spacecraft fighter pilots and starship crews in combat.
values.jedi_sith: Jedi, Sith and other laser-sword wielders.
values.mutants_superpowered: Mutants or people with powers who are not costumed heroes.
values.apes_animals: Apes and other animals as fighters.
values.civilians: Ordinary people caught in the action.
values.stunt_hero: A lone hero performing a stunt.

weapons.label: Weapons
weapons.description: Weapons visible in use. Empty when nobody fights.

values.superpowers: Super strength, energy blasts, telekinesis, speed.
values.vehicle_as_weapon: Ramming with cars, trucks or ships.

vehicles.label: Vehicles
vehicles.description: Vehicles and mounts that feature in the action.

values.warship: Powered military ships: warships, troopships and naval transports.
values.civilian_ship: Large non-military ship: freighter, tanker, liner, cruise ship, ferry, trawler.
values.capital_ship: Large spaceships, cruisers, star destroyers, space stations.
values.lunar_planetary_vehicle: Landers, rovers, ornithopters, shuttles to a surface.

technique.label: Filmmaking technique
technique.description: Craft worth studying in this scene.

values.long_take: Unbroken or apparently unbroken shot (a 'oner'), including stitched long takes.
values.tracking_shot: Camera moving alongside the action (dolly, car mount, cable cam).
values.wide_framing: Wide shots that let the choreography play without cutting.
values.center_framing: Action held in the centre of the frame for fast readability.
values.vehicle_stunts: Real car, bike or truck stunts.
values.practical_effects: Physical effects on set (squibs, animatronics, rigs).
values.wire_work: Wires and harnesses for flying or falls.
values.undercranking: Shot at lower frame rate to speed up the action.
values.fast_cutting: Rapid editing and shaky, fragmented coverage.
values.score_driven: Cut or paced to music or score.
values.silence: Silence or near-silence used for effect.
values.large_crowds: Large numbers of real extras or crowd simulation.

violence.label: On-screen violence
violence.description: How graphic the clip is, for choosing what to show whom.

values.mild: Action without blood or with stylised impacts.
values.moderate: Visible injuries or deaths without lingering gore.

language.label: Original language
language.description: Main spoken language of the original version.

values.none_or_minimal: No meaningful dialogue (silent films, wordless scenes).
